The Committee contends that implementation of the proposed expansion of commercial zones and terminal areas will have numerous adverse effects, including: (1) creation of unnecessary additional carriers, (2) injury to small shippers through the relinquishment of Commission jurisdiction, (3) proliferation of hazardous operations in urban areas, (4) excessive drain on energy resources and harm to the environment, (5) acceleration of central city decay and other urban planning problems, and (6) devastating economic effects on existing regulated short haul carriers.
The Committee's brief concludes by requesting oral and regional hearings to resolve the important and controversial issues involved in this proceeding.
Freight Forwarder Representations. - In their representations filed in response to the original rulemaking notice, which are summarized in the Interim Report, Commercial Zones, 124 M.C.C. at 152-54, the forwarders argue that economic growth coupled with the convenience of modern expressways and beltways have caused metropolitan areas to expand far beyond their terminal areas. They have lost the traffic of shippers which have moved beyond their terminal areas and have been unable to obtain a reasonable share of new traffic. The movement of business and industrial activity to outlying suburban areas has greatly increased freight forwarder reliance on regulated motor carriers.
